what: Known-item check: photographs of KIND listing 8001001141404 must return that listing.
result: SOURCE LISTING NOT IN PUBLIC TABS
diagnosis: The target is never retrieved. Its listing id appears zero times anywhere in the campaign log, so it is absent from the candidate set rather than present and ranked low, and absent rather than present and hidden. Four candidates were hidden and none of them is the target.
why_this_narrows_it: The finding was carried as 'photographs of a listing do not return that listing', which reads as a matching failure. It is not one. The matcher never sees the listing. Work on item matching, thresholds or the Real gate cannot move this; the listing has to be discovered first.
next: Establish why the KIND catalogue walk does not surface this product for these queries: whether the query family never names it, whether the walk stops before reaching its page, or whether it is fetched and dropped during normalisation.
also_observed: coverage reported pages_charged_to_page_limit: null on this path. The field was added today and reads the budget ledger; null means the ledger was absent here, which is reported as absence rather than as zero, but it means the page limit is still not checkable on this route.

root_cause.target_is_live: https://shop.kind.co.jp/products/8001001141404.json returns a published product with 5 images
root_cause.title: 無地 ロングスリーブカットソー - a plain long-sleeve cut-and-sew. No brand, no model, no year.
root_cause.not_in_catalogue_head: Absent from the first 2000 products of products.json (8 pages x 250, scanned in order).
root_cause.why_it_is_never_retrieved: Two independent reasons, either of which alone is sufficient. No query family can name it: the compiled queries are built from brand, model, line and year, and this listing has none of those - its title is a generic garment noun. And the catalogue walk cannot reach it: it is beyond 2000 products in feed order, far past any bounded page budget.
root_cause.what_this_means: Discovery is text-driven, and image matching only runs on candidates discovery already returned. An item whose listing carries no distinguishing text is therefore unreachable no matter how good the matcher is. This is one architectural gap rather than two defects, and it explains the known-item miss and the retrieval-quality score together.
root_cause.not_a_reason_to_retire_the_check: The scenario is the product's core promise - photograph something you own, find its listing. The check failing is correct. What it shows is that the promise needs visual retrieval over a source's catalogue, not better ranking of text-retrieved candidates.

closed: search_listings_by_descriptor: cosine over stored image descriptors, dimension-guarded, best-photograph-per-listing
WarmIndex.search merges descriptor hits into the rows instead of only rescoring text hits
consult_and_surface builds its query descriptor from the campaign's reference photographs rather than a hashed text vector

remaining_spec.problem: The warm index is populated by remember_campaign from candidates a campaign already retrieved. A listing text never named was never indexed, so descriptor search cannot find it: the visual route now works but has nothing to search.
remaining_spec.what_to_build: A pass that walks an admitted source's catalogue feed and indexes each product with its image descriptors, independently of any campaign query. The machinery exists - catalog_feed_path_of, build_catalog_page_url and catalog_caps_from_env in searcher/sources/catalog.py already page a Shopify feed, and WarmIndex.put_listing already accepts descriptors.
remaining_spec.acceptance: ./scripts/known_item_check.sh returns KIND listing 8001001141404 in Real or Possibly Real. That listing is the test because it is unreachable by text: a plain long-sleeve cut-and-sew with no brand, model, line or year, sitting past 2000 items in feed order.
remaining_spec.constraints: Robots must still be honoured, the ingest must be bounded by the same budget discipline as discovery, and indexing must not be triggered per-campaign or every search pays for a catalogue walk.
remaining_spec.verify_the_caller_not_the_component: Five findings today were reported working after verifying a component and not the path that calls it. Before claiming this closed, run the live check rather than a unit test of the ingest function.

end_to_end_visual_retrieval.what: The visual route exercised on real data, with no text query involved.
end_to_end_visual_retrieval.method: Ingested all 250 products of shop.kind.co.jp products.json page 9 - the page carrying the target - describing one image each. Queried with fixtures/user_snapshots/8001001141404_snapshot.jpg, a simulated user photograph of the target item.
end_to_end_visual_retrieval.why_this_matters: The listing carries no brand, model, line or year, so no compiled query can name it, and it sits past 2000 items so no bounded catalogue walk reaches it. It was retrieved by its photographs against 250 real competing products. The route works end to end.
end_to_end_visual_retrieval.the_honest_limit: descriptor_from_bytes returned a 24-dimension descriptor, not the 384-dimension DINOv2 embedding. That is a cheap fallback, and it shows: the top five scores sit between 0.969 and 0.995, so the ranking is barely separated. Rank 2 of 250 is the fallback's result, not the model's. Running this path on the real embedding is the next lever and is likely worth the rank-1 place.
end_to_end_visual_retrieval.what_is_still_not_done: The live known-item check runs a full campaign and needs a walk reaching feed position 2095 with the real model. This proves the mechanism and quantifies the depth; it does not replace that run.

with_real_embedding.change: descriptor_from_bytes now returns the DINOv2 embedding when weights resolve, colour histogram otherwise.

before.reading: a 0.026 spread across five listings is not separation; rank 2 there was close to arbitrary

with_real_embedding.reading: The item nothing can name is now retrieved first from its photographs, against 250 real competing products, with the runners-up 0.035 behind rather than 0.019. The index was storing colour histograms while the embedding sat behind pair_similarity, unused by the index path.
with_real_embedding.safety_of_the_change: Descriptors of different dimensions never meet: search_listings_by_descriptor skips a mismatch rather than comparing across spaces, so an index written by the histogram and queried by the embedding finds nothing rather than nonsense.

full_depth_run.what: The known-item target retrieved from a catalogue indexed to the depth it actually sits at.
full_depth_run.reading: A listing carrying no brand, model, line or year - unnameable by any compiled query - retrieved first from a photograph against 2250 real competing products from the same shop. This is the full catalogue depth the target sits at, not a slice chosen to contain it.
full_depth_run.still_not_run: scripts/known_item_check.sh drives a full campaign against a live API and has not been run. This measures the retrieval route directly. The two are different tests and the campaign one remains the acceptance.

live_check_run.result: SOURCE LISTING NOT IN PUBLIC TABS - the check still fails

preconditions_verified.versions_match: stored model_version histogram-1 / adapter_version listing-index-1 equals versions_from_settings
preconditions_verified.descriptor_dimensions_align: ingest and query both use descriptor_from_bytes, 384

live_check_run.direct_route_works: The same query against the same index returns the target at rank 1 of 2250.
live_check_run.conclusion: Every precondition that can be checked from outside is satisfied and the campaign still does not surface the listing, so the remaining gap is inside consult_and_surface or hydrate_from_index rather than in the index, the descriptors or the query. That has not been isolated and is not claimed as understood.
live_check_run.next: Instrument consult_and_surface on this campaign: whether index.search returns the target among its hits, and if it does, what hydrate_from_index does with it. The direct search proves the data and the query are right, so the loss is downstream of both.

isolated.conclusion: The target survives retrieval and becomes one of 63 candidates, then is cut before judgment: only 8 candidates were scored at all, 4 hidden and 4 possibly real, and the target is not among them. It was never judged and never hidden - it was dropped by whatever selects which candidates get scored.
isolated.what_this_rules_out: Not retrieval: the consult path returns it among 40 hits with a 384-dimension query built from the user's photographs. Not the Real gate, the screening gate, or any veto: no judgment ran on it. Not the index, the descriptors, the versions or the dimensions, all verified aligned.
isolated.next: Find the shortlist that admits 8 of 63 candidates to judgment and why the target is outside it. Likely a deep-matching or part-matching cap applied on a text-derived ordering, which would place a visually-retrieved candidate last by construction.

root_cause_final.mechanism: FINE_COMPARE_CAP = 8 in campaigns/orchestrator.py. select_kept_ids admits the ranked candidates first, then fills by discovery order, and never exceeds the cap.
root_cause_final.which_path_ran: Routing was not blocked, so the ranked path ran rather than the degraded discovery-order fallback. Broad retrieval produced a ranking and the target did not reach its top 8.
root_cause_final.conclusion: The shortlist is doing its job on a ranking that fails. The same item the warm index returns at rank 1 of 2250 on its photographs is ranked outside the top 8 of 63 by broad retrieval, which decides what gets scored. Visual similarity retrieves it and then does not carry into the ordering that admits candidates to judgment.
root_cause_final.the_fix_is_not_the_cap: Raising the cap would let this listing through and would not fix the ordering; the next item with no matching text would sit at position 31. Broad retrieval has to weigh the visual evidence that already found the item.

actual_mechanism.explanation: A candidate hydrated from the warm index carries image metadata but no image bytes: nothing fetched them into the campaign's content store. `_candidate_pngs` therefore returns an empty map for it, broad retrieval has no pixels to compare, its visual score is empty, and it ranks below candidates whose images were fetched during discovery. The cap of 8 then cuts it.
actual_mechanism.why_this_supersedes_the_earlier_reading: The previous note said broad retrieval ranks it poorly and needs to weigh visual evidence. It cannot weigh what it does not have. The ordering is not mis-weighted; the input is missing.
two_possible_repairs: Fetch the images for an index-hydrated candidate before broad retrieval, which costs a download per candidate and makes it comparable to a discovered one.
Carry the index's own descriptor similarity through as a prior, which costs nothing because the index already computed it - the same score that ranked the target 1 of 2250.
actual_mechanism.not_yet_attempted: Neither repair is implemented. The mechanism is measured, not fixed.

confirmed_in_code.what: It copies each image's metadata - content_digest and remote_url survive - and assigns fresh ids, but it never fetches bytes. Its first statement is `del search_id`, so it cannot address the campaign's content store even in principle. An index-hydrated candidate is pixel-less by construction, not by accident.
confirmed_in_code.matches_the_measurement: 5 images on the candidate, 0 retrievable bytes.
confirmed_in_code.where_a_repair_belongs: hydrate_from_index holds the controller and therefore the store. Fetching each image's remote_url there and writing it under its content_digest would make the candidate comparable. It needs the same robots and budget discipline as discovery, which is why it is not a two-line change and is not attempted here.

RESOLVED.the_fix: _download_listing_image skipped any image that already carried a content_digest. That is sound for a candidate this campaign discovered and downloaded, and wrong for one hydrated from the warm index, where the digest is copied from the stored payload while the bytes live in whichever campaign first indexed them. A digest was being read as proof of possession. It now also checks the bytes are retrievable from this campaign's store, and fails closed - an unreadable store means a redundant download rather than a pixel-less candidate.
RESOLVED.why_it_was_hard_to_see: Every layer reported success. Ingest indexed 2250 listings. The index returned the target at rank 1 of 2250. Consult carried it into the campaign among 40 hits. It became candidate 30 of 63. Nothing failed, and the item still never reached judgment, because one boolean treated metadata as data.

after_orchestrator_screening.check: PASS - target ranked 1 in Possibly Real
after_orchestrator_screening.reading: Screening now runs on the live path, so Real is no longer shut by an unscreened candidate. It is shut by the evidence: item match is 0.863 against 0.90 and authenticity is 0.231 against 0.80. Both are genuine measurements of a real listing rather than an artefact of a gate nothing satisfied.
after_orchestrator_screening.and_by_the_documented_scope_limit: This listing is a garment, so its authenticity interval is uncalibrated - only designer_footwear ships a table - and ranking/buckets.py caps an uncalibrated candidate below the Real gate regardless of its evidence. Real is therefore unreachable for this item by policy as well as by evidence.
after_orchestrator_screening.what_changed_and_what_did_not: Changed: screening runs, so the theft veto is reachable and Real is not blocked by an unanswerable precondition. Unchanged: this item cannot be Real, and saying so is the product working rather than failing.
